gallery.caption: Your phone camera was built for space
gallery.alt: Reel cover: Your phone camera was built for space. Well, the chip inside it was. An illustration of a phone's camera.

gallery.caption: A day on Venus is longer than its year
gallery.alt: Strange but true: 243 is greater than 225. A day on Venus, 243 Earth days, is longer than its year of 225 days, and Venus spins backward.

gallery.caption: That's not a star: Saturn at its brightest
gallery.alt: Reel cover: That's not a star. Look east tonight at 9:30 p.m. A star chart shows Saturn above the east-southeast horizon.

gallery.caption: Find Saturn at its brightest
gallery.alt: Star chart: find Saturn at its brightest on Saturday, October 3 at 9:30 p.m. local time. Face east-southeast, look about three fists up, and the steady golden light is Saturn.

gallery.caption: There are mirrors on the Moon
gallery.alt: Reel cover: There are mirrors on the Moon, and scientists still use them. A laser beam travels from Earth to the Moon.

gallery.caption: The sound that scared America in 1957
gallery.alt: Reel cover: This sound scared America. A green waveform of Sputnik's radio beep, October 4, 1957.

gallery.caption: Earth and the Moon, to scale
gallery.alt: True to scale: if Earth were a 1-inch marble, the Moon would be a pea 30 inches away. Earth is 7,918 miles wide, the Moon 2,159, and they're 238,855 miles apart.

gallery.caption: Saturday is Saturn's day
gallery.alt: Reel cover: Saturday equals Saturn's day. And the rest of your week? An illustration of Saturn and its rings.

gallery.caption: NASA didn't invent Velcro
gallery.alt: Reel cover: NASA didn't invent Velcro. The claim 'NASA invented Velcro' is stamped MYTH: a Swiss engineer got the idea from burrs on his dog in 1941.

gallery.caption: Apollo 11's computer had about 4 KB of memory
gallery.alt: Strange but true: 4 KB. Apollo 11's guidance computer had about 4 kilobytes of working memory, and its programs lived in hand-woven core rope memory.

gallery.caption: The dark side of the Moon isn't dark
gallery.alt: Reel cover: The dark side of the Moon isn't dark. 67 years ago today, we first saw it. A diagram shows sunlight reaching the Moon's far side.
